chunks: Tafsir al-Qummi: From him (Ibrahim ibn Hashim) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhayna from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) concerning His words:
“Non of the angered upon them and non of the astray”
He said: The Maghdub Alayhim (those angered upon) are the Nussab (haters of the Ahl al-Bayt), and the Dhalin (the astray) are the Shakkak (doubters) who do not know the Imam.

key_terms.الشَّكَّاكُ: The doubters (those uncertain about religious authority)
key_terms.الْمَغْضُوبَ عَلَيْهِمُ: The angered upon (those who know the truth but reject it)

ai.seo_question: Who are the Maghdub Alayhim and Dhalin according to Shia tafsir?
ai.summary: This narration from Tafsir al-Qummi, transmitted through the chain of Ibn Abi 'Umayr, offers a distinct Shia exegetical interpretation of Surah Al-Fatiha by linking the 'Maghdub Alayhim' to the 'Nussab' (those bearing enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) and the 'Dhalin' to the 'Shakkak' (doubters who fail to recognize the Imam). This reading underscores the centrality of Imamate in Shia theology, suggesting that spiritual deviation is fundamentally tied to the recognition of divine authority. Such interpretations highlight the Shia emphasis on the continuity of guidance through the Imams as the criterion for true faith.
